I experienced sleep paralysis last night for the fifth time in my life. As it is an uncommon occurrence for me, it took me awhile to make a connection between the type of dream I was experiencing and the paralysis.

Fortunately (or unfortunately) every instance was preceded by a fairly disturbing dream, so I am able to clearly recall even the two that occurred during my childhood.

4 out of the 5 were identical in subject matter. They all began as a typical rambling dream which sequed into something more stressful until at the end something demonic and humanoid (dead eyes, twisted facial features, radiating malice) reached out to grab me.

A few years ago, I woke up from one of these dreams and actually saw a humanoid shadow hovering in front of me. This was the most terrifying of the four dreams involving the demonic.

The fifth dream, I hesitate to even call a dream, although at the time I thought it was just a really bad nightmare. I woke from that one disturbed enough to wake my husband for consolation.

It involved driving through the countryside where most of my extended family live. Pulling into a parking lot and seeing an ambulance. In the front passenger seat was one of my cousins bawling. She kept asking me where her sister was.

I walked around the back and there was a body covered in a sheet. Then the dream immediately cut to me riding in the back seat of a car that was speeding around hairpin curves on a road I was familiarish with. One of my aunts was driving. My mom was riding shotgun. My grandmother (who was recently deceased irl) was riding in the back beside me.

I was screaming for my aunt to slow down when a truck appeared in front of us and we collided. I saw white and woke up paralyzed.

The reason I say it was not a normal nightmare is because I received a call two days later from my mom to tell me that the missing sister from my dream had died the night before. It was instantaneous. Her friend was driving too fast on a curvy road, crossed the median, and collided with a truck. She was sitting in the same seat as I was when she died. She was alone in the back seat, but I like to think that my grandmother was really there beside her.

I have had a lot of nightmares in my life. I actually enjoy the scare most of the time. Kind of like visiting a haunted house at Halloween, only without the entry fee.

However only a tiny percentage of these heart racing dreams have resulted in waking to sleep paralysis, and all five have had a spiritual context to the dream.

I have never experienced sleep paralysis when waking from a regular dream - not even after stress dreams (teeth falling out, lost the kid in the store, etc).

So in the interest of proving my theory, to myself at least, I would love to hear read any of you Goats' experiences with sleep paralysis.

I have had quite a few as well. What happens to me is that I have some sort of dream that shocks my body into a state of mild awareness. I recognize where I am and my sleeping position. At some unknown interval my brain moves from awareness into dreamland again, but I start the dream in the location and position in which I am.

This is incredibly unsettling in scary dreams, and wonderfully expansive in pleasant dreams. I find it interesting that even though the dream starts in a well-established and known place, almost immediately the geometry of the surroundings is warped in some way. I've never had a dream that coincided with real world consequences from what I can tell.

For me, the wildest part is that these happen to me in tightly wound loops. A sleep paralysis dream-loop will pull me into 6 or 7 dreams, all starting in the same location and pose. It makes waking up for real a mindbending experience because everything that preceded felt tactile.

Also, I'm sad to hear about your loss. Hope you and your family can bear the burden together.
